newsitem.title: USA: Savannah Foods says merger to feed growth.
newsitem.headline: Savannah Foods says merger to feed growth.

text.p: The merger of sugar refiner Savannah Foods & Industries Inc with privately held sugar producer Florida Crystals Inc will create an integrated sugar business set for growth, the companies said on Tuesday.
Alfonso Fanjul, chairman and chief executive of Florida Crystal, said the new company will look to boost shareholder value through cost savings and strategic acquisitions.
"We think we can grow the company over the next few years," Fanjul told reporters in a conference call briefing.
Fanjul, who will hold the same posts in the new company, and Savannah Foods president William Sprague, declined to value the transaction announced earlier on Tuesday.
The new entity will have annual revenues on a pro-forma basis of about $1.5 billion and assets above $1 billion.

But the officials said the new company will be the first in the U.S. to include operations in growing, milling and refining of sugar, and will account for about 20 percent of the U.S. refined sugar market.
"By vertically integrating and combining a raw sugar company with a refiner, we really get the best of both worlds," Sprague told reporters.

"This is a continuation of the strategic plan announced to shareholders over a year ago to maximize the value of existing sugar business and grow related companies to become a multi-billion dollar company for the future," Sprague said.
Savannah is one of the largest refiners of cane and beet sugar in the United States.

Sprague, who will be president of the new company's sugar division, said the merger is not expected to cause significant layoffs. Savings will come from streamlining purchasing, freight and transport costs, and lowering working capital costs through direct access to raw sugar production, he said.
The new company will be known initially as Savannah Food Industries.
Florida Crystals farms 180,000 acres and produces more than 640,000 tons of raw cane sugar annually. The company also operates two sugar mills and one refinery in Palm Beach County, Fla.
Florida Crystals is a subsidiary of privately-held Flo-Sun Inc of Florida, a diversified agricultural, real estate and resort company.

Flo-Sun Inc will hold 39.4 percent of the equity in the merged company, other Florida Crystals shareholders will hold 19.1 percent of the equity, and Savannah Foods' shareholders will hold the remaining 41.5 percent, the company said.
The merger is subject to the approval of the Savannah Foods' shareholders and is expected to close in October.
